title: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes
description: Grade 12 Biology: what biotechnology is, the tools of recombinant DNA technology (enzymes, vectors, hosts), and the steps of making recombinant DNA and gene cloning.

topics.title: What Is Biotechnology?
topics.concept:
Biotechnology is the use of living organisms (or their parts, like cells and enzymes) to make useful products and services for humans. Humans have used a simple form of biotechnology for thousands of years — for example, using yeast to make bread and microbes to make curd. But modern biotechnology is much more powerful because it can change the very genes of an organism.

The heart of modern biotechnology is genetic engineering, also called recombinant DNA (rDNA) technology. This means changing the genetic make-up of an organism by adding, removing or altering specific genes. A piece of useful DNA from one organism can be joined to the DNA of another, creating recombinant DNA. An organism that has received a foreign gene in this way is called a genetically modified organism (GMO) or transgenic organism.

Why is this so useful? Because it lets us give organisms new, desirable traits — for example, putting the human insulin gene into bacteria so they make human insulin for diabetics, or putting a pest-resistance gene into crops. Modern biotechnology has two core techniques: genetic engineering (creating recombinant DNA and GMOs) and the large-scale growth of cells/microbes in big vessels called bioreactors to make the product in useful amounts. Together these have transformed medicine, agriculture and industry.

examples.solution:
It uses living things for products.

  • Biotechnology is the use of living organisms (or their parts) to make useful products and services.
examples.answer: Biotechnology is the use of living organisms or their parts to make useful products and services for humans.

examples.solution:
It combines DNA from two sources.

  • Recombinant DNA is DNA made by joining a piece of DNA from one organism to that of another.
examples.answer: Recombinant DNA is DNA formed by joining DNA from two different sources (a foreign gene into another organism's DNA).

examples.problem: Example 3: Give one example of a useful product of genetic engineering.
examples.solution:
Think of a medicine made by modified bacteria.

  • Human insulin made by bacteria carrying the human insulin gene.
examples.answer: Human insulin produced by bacteria that have been given the human insulin gene.

recap:
• Biotechnology = using living organisms/their parts to make useful products (old: curd, bread; modern: changing genes).
  • Core = genetic engineering / recombinant DNA (rDNA) technology: add/remove/alter genes → recombinant DNA, GMO/transgenic organisms.
  • Two key techniques: genetic engineering + large-scale growth in bioreactors.
  • Uses: human insulin in bacteria, pest-resistant crops, etc.

quiz.q: An organism that has received a foreign gene is called a:
quiz.explanation: An organism with a foreign gene is a genetically modified (transgenic) organism.

quiz.q: DNA made by joining DNA from two different sources is:
quiz.explanation: Recombinant DNA combines DNA from two sources.

topics.title: Tools of Recombinant DNA Technology
topics.concept:
To cut, join, copy and move genes, scientists use a set of special biological tools. The three most important groups are enzymes, vectors and host cells.

  • Enzymes — molecular 'tools' that act on DNA:
    • Restriction enzymes are the "molecular scissors" that cut DNA at specific sequences. Because they cut at particular sites, a gene of interest can be cut out precisely.
    • DNA ligase is the "molecular glue" that joins two pieces of DNA together (it seals the cut gene into the vector).
  • Vectors — carriers that take the foreign gene into a host cell. The most common are plasmids (small, circular pieces of DNA found in bacteria, separate from the main chromosome) and certain viruses. A good vector can replicate inside the host and usually carries a marker so that cells which took up the gene can be identified.
  • Host cell — the living cell (often the bacterium E. coli) into which the recombinant DNA is put; here the gene is copied and expressed.

So restriction enzymes cut the DNA, ligase joins the desired gene into a plasmid vector, and the vector carries it into a host cell — these tools together make gene manipulation possible. The same enzyme that cuts the gene of interest is used to cut the vector, so that their ends match and can be joined.

examples.problem: Example 1: What is the role of restriction enzymes?
examples.solution:
They cut DNA.

  • Restriction enzymes are 'molecular scissors' that cut DNA at specific sequences.
examples.answer: Restriction enzymes act as molecular scissors that cut DNA at specific sequences.

examples.solution:
It joins DNA.

  • DNA ligase is the 'molecular glue' that joins two pieces of DNA.
examples.answer: DNA ligase joins two pieces of DNA together (it seals the gene into the vector).

examples.problem: Example 3: What is a vector, and name the most common one.
examples.solution:
It carries the gene into a cell.

  • A vector carries the foreign gene into a host cell.
  • The most common is a plasmid.
examples.answer: A vector is a carrier that takes the foreign gene into a host cell; the most common is a plasmid.

recap:
• Restriction enzymes = molecular scissors (cut DNA at specific sites); DNA ligase = molecular glue (joins DNA).
  • Vectors (carry the gene in): plasmids (bacterial circular DNA) and some viruses; carry a marker.
  • Host cell (e.g. E. coli): where rDNA is copied and expressed.
  • Same restriction enzyme cuts both gene and vector so ends match.

quiz.q: The 'molecular scissors' that cut DNA at specific sites are:
quiz.explanation: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sequences.

quiz.q: A small circular piece of bacterial DNA used as a vector is a:
quiz.explanation: Plasmids are circular bacterial DNA used as vectors.

topics.title: Making Recombinant DNA and Gene Cloning
topics.concept:
Putting the tools together, recombinant DNA technology follows a logical series of steps to make and multiply a desired gene:

  1. Isolating the DNA — the DNA containing the gene of interest is extracted from the source organism's cells.
  2. Cutting the DNA — restriction enzymes cut out the desired gene, and the same enzyme cuts open the vector (plasmid), so their ends match.
  3. Joining (ligation) — DNA ligase glues the gene into the plasmid, forming the recombinant DNA.
  4. Inserting into a host — the recombinant plasmid is put into a host cell (often E. coli); the cell takes it up (transformation).
  5. Multiplying (cloning) — the host cell, grown in a culture, divides again and again, and every daughter cell carries a copy of the gene. Making many identical copies of a gene (or organism) is called cloning. Grown on a large scale in a bioreactor, the cells can make large amounts of the gene's product.
  6. Obtaining the product — finally the desired product (such as a protein/medicine) is extracted and purified — this last stage is called downstream processing.

A separate but related tool is the Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), a technique that makes millions of copies of a specific piece of DNA quickly in a test tube. PCR is widely used in research, in diagnosing diseases and in forensics. Together, these processes let scientists produce valuable proteins, modify crops and study genes — the practical power of biotechnology.

In short, the standard steps of genetic engineering are: isolation of the DNA, cutting it with restriction enzymes, amplification by PCR, gene transfer of the recombinant DNA into a host cell, and finally the expression of the gene so that the host makes the desired product.

examples.problem: Example 1: List, in order, the main steps of making recombinant DNA.
examples.solution:
Follow the logical sequence.

  • Isolate DNA → cut with restriction enzyme → join gene into vector with ligase → insert into host → multiply (clone) → obtain product.
examples.answer: Isolate DNA → cut with restriction enzymes → ligate the gene into a vector → insert into a host → clone (multiply) → extract the product.

examples.problem: Example 2: What is cloning in this context?
examples.solution:
It means making many identical copies.

  • Cloning is making many identical copies of a gene (or organism).
  • Here, the host cell divides so every daughter carries the gene.
examples.answer: Cloning is making many identical copies of a gene (or organism) — the host cell divides, copying the gene each time.

examples.problem: Example 3: What does PCR do, and give one use.
examples.solution:
PCR amplifies DNA.

  • PCR makes millions of copies of a specific DNA piece quickly.
  • It is used in disease diagnosis and forensics.
examples.answer: PCR rapidly makes millions of copies of a specific DNA segment; it is used in diagnosis and forensics.

recap:
• rDNA steps: isolate DNA → cut (restriction enzyme) → ligate gene into vector → insert into host (transformation) → clone (multiply) → obtain product (downstream processing).
  • Cloning = many identical copies; large-scale growth in a bioreactor.
  • PCR: makes millions of copies of a DNA segment fast; used in diagnosis, research, forensics.

quiz.explanation: Cloning produces many identical copies of a gene/organism.

questions.q: Biotechnology is the use of ____ to make useful products.
questions.explanation: Biotechnology uses living organisms or their parts.

questions.q: An old example of biotechnology is making:
questions.explanation: Using microbes to make curd is a traditional biotechnology.

questions.q: Changing the genes of an organism is called:
questions.explanation: Genetic engineering alters an organism's genes.

questions.q: DNA made by joining DNA from two sources is:
questions.explanation: Recombinant DNA combines DNA from two sources.

questions.q: An organism with a foreign gene is called a:
questions.explanation: Such an organism is genetically modified (transgenic).

questions.q: Restriction enzymes act as:
questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific sites.

questions.q: The enzyme that joins two pieces of DNA is:
questions.explanation: DNA ligase glues DNA pieces together.

questions.q: A common vector used to carry genes is a:
questions.explanation: Plasmids are commonly used as vectors.

questions.q: A plasmid is a small ____ piece of bacterial DNA.
questions.explanation: Plasmids are small circular DNA molecules in bacteria.

questions.q: A commonly used host cell in genetic engineering is:
questions.explanation: The bacterium E. coli is a common host cell.

questions.q: The same restriction enzyme is used on the gene and the vector so that their:
options: Cut ends match and can be joined
questions.explanation: Matching cut ends allow the gene to be ligated into the vector.

questions.q: Making many identical copies of a gene is:
questions.explanation: Cloning produces identical copies.

questions.q: Large-scale growth of cells to make a product happens in a:
questions.explanation: Bioreactors grow cells on a large scale.

questions.q: Extracting and purifying the final product is called:
questions.explanation: Downstream processing recovers and purifies the product.

questions.q: PCR is a technique used to:
options: Make many copies of a DNA segment
questions.explanation: PCR amplifies a specific DNA segment millions of times.

questions.q: Producing human insulin in bacteria is valuable because the bacteria can:
options: Make large amounts of exactly human insulin cheaply
questions.explanation: Transgenic bacteria mass-produce true human insulin, safer and more plentiful than animal sources.

questions.q: Using the SAME restriction enzyme on both the gene and the plasmid is essential because it creates:
options: Matching (complementary) ends that ligase can join
questions.explanation: Identical cut sites give compatible ends, so the gene fits and ligase seals it into the vector.

questions.q: A marker gene on a plasmid is useful because it helps scientists:
options: Identify host cells that took up the recombinant DNA
questions.explanation: The marker lets researchers select only the cells that successfully received the recombinant plasmid.

questions.q: Cloning the host cell in a bioreactor matters because each daughter cell:
options: Carries a copy of the gene and makes more product
questions.explanation: Every division copies the gene, so a large culture yields large amounts of the desired product.

questions.q: PCR is especially useful in diagnosing an infection early because it can detect a pathogen from:
options: Even a tiny amount of its DNA by amplifying it
questions.explanation: By multiplying minute traces of pathogen DNA, PCR enables detection long before large numbers build up.

questions.q: DNA ligase is aptly called molecular glue because, unlike restriction enzymes, it:
options: Joins DNA fragments rather than cutting them
questions.explanation: Restriction enzymes cut; ligase performs the opposite job of sealing fragments together.
